questions.question: What does `tool_choice: auto` mean in the Claude API?
options: Claude must call some tool, but can pick which one
Claude decides for itself whether calling a tool is appropriate, and if so, which one
Claude is forced to call a specific named tool
Claude is prevented from calling any tool

questions.question: What is the difference between `tool_choice: any` and `tool_choice` with a specific tool `name`?
options: There is no difference, they behave identically
`any` forces some tool call but lets Claude pick which one; a named tool forces that exact tool regardless of what the input suggests
`any` prevents tool calls entirely; a named tool allows any tool
`any` only works with a single tool defined; named tool_choice requires multiple tools

questions.question: In a structured-extraction step where a free-text answer would break the downstream pipeline, which `tool_choice` approach fits best?
options: `none`, so Claude responds in plain prose only
Forcing a specific tool (or `any`) for that turn so Claude can't just respond in prose instead
Leaving it on `auto` for every turn of the conversation
Removing all tools from the request

questions.question: What is the common pattern for using forced tool_choice across a multi-turn conversation?
options: Keep tool_choice forced for the entire conversation to guarantee structured output at every turn
Force a specific tool for exactly the one turn that needs it, then switch back to `auto` afterward
Force a tool only on the last turn of the conversation
Never use forced tool_choice in multi-turn conversations

questions.question: What goes wrong if `tool_choice` is left forced across an entire multi-turn conversation rather than switched back to `auto`?
options: Nothing, it's always safe to leave forced indefinitely
Claude would never be able to respond in plain text again for the rest of the conversation
The API would start rejecting all subsequent requests
Claude would ignore the forced tool after the first turn anyway

questions.question: What does `tool_choice: none` do?
options: Removes all tools from the request payload
Claude must not call a tool on this turn, even if one is available and would normally be used
Claude must call every available tool at once
It has the same effect as omitting tool_choice entirely
